title: 2021 Fall AMC 10B Problem 22
statement: For each integer \(n\ge2,\) let \(S_n\) be the sum of all products \(jk,\) where \(j\) and \(k\) are integers and \(1\le j<k\le n.\) What is the sum of the \(10\) least values of \(n\) such that \(S_n\) is divisible by \(3?\)

solutions.text:
When passing from \(S_{n-1}\) to \(S_n,\) the new terms are \(jn\) for \(1\le j\lt n.\) Their sum is \[ \begin{gathered} n(1+2+\cdots+(n-1))\\ =\frac{n^2(n-1)}2. \end{gathered} \]

Modulo \(3,\) this increment is \(0\) when \(n\equiv0\) or \(1\pmod3,\) and is \(2\) when \(n\equiv2\pmod3.\)

Since \(S_2=2,\) the sequence becomes divisible by \(3\) after the third occurrence of a number congruent to \(2\pmod3,\) namely at \(n=8.\) Then \(S_n\) stays divisible by \(3\) for \(n=8,9,10,\) and the same pattern repeats every \(9\) in \(n.\)

The ten least values are \(8,9,10,17,18,19,26,27,28,35.\) Their sum is \(197.\)

Thus, the answer is B .
